item_3.notes: [chunk 1/1] Item 3 (Legal Proceedings) contains extensive regulatory and litigation risk disclosures but NO material SIFI-relevant entities, counterparty relationships, investments, acquisitions, capex commitments, or off-balance-sheet structures. The filing discloses: (1) Privacy/data protection litigation (FTC settlement $5B, IDPC €1.2B fine, California settlement pending); (2) Antitrust/competition cases (FTC antitrust case resolved in Meta's favor 11/2025, class actions, European Commission fines €798M and €200M); (3) Youth-related product liability and COPPA claims; (4) Copyright/AI training litigation; (5) DSA/regulatory compliance proceedings. The litigation concerns business practices, algorithms, user data, content moderation, and advertising practices—all operational and reputational, not structural financial risks. Meta's dividend policy (declared 2024, $4.60B Class A / $720M Class B in 2025) is disclosed but represents shareholder distribution, not SIFI material debt or leverage. No infrastructure partnerships, capex commitments to counterparties, or hidden financial arrangements are mentioned. Per HARD RULE 3, generic litigation, regulatory fines, and procedural risks are excluded unless they disclose hidden leverage, circularity, revenue roundtripping, capex gaps, or material concentration. This section is boilerplate legal risk and should be skipped.

item_7.notes:
[chunk 1/2] This is Item 7 (MD&A) only — no notes to financial statements were included in the source text. Key extractions:

1. CAPEX: $72.22B actual spend FY2025 (including finance lease payments), directed at AI infrastructure and data centers. No specific counterparty named for the bulk of this spend in this section.

2. CAPEX ROI GAP (severity 3): $72.22B capex with RL generating -$19.19B operating loss and no revenue ramp disclosed. RL losses guided flat into 2026 with no timeline to profitability.

3. COST OPACITY (severity 3): Server/network asset useful life extended from implied prior level to 5.5 years effective Jan 1, 2025 — a classic earnings-smoothing mechanism that reduces annual depreciation, inflating near-term profits. Magnitude of the earnings impact is NOT quantified in this section (would need Note 1 for the dollar amount).

4. COST OPACITY (severity 2): Non-marketable equity investment fair value adjustments may lag actual transaction timing — creates a period-mismatch risk in reported investment gains/losses. Note 5 referenced for detail not included here.

5. No SPV/off-balance-sheet entities, specific AI lab investments, or named compute-supply counterparties are disclosed in this MD&A section. Those details would appear in Item 8 notes (Note 5, Note 11). The Hyperion/Blue Owl structure referenced in prior filings would need to be confirmed in the current filing's notes.

6. Apple and Google named as counterparties adversely affecting ad-targeting capability via iOS and browser changes — SIFI-material because substantially all of Meta's $198.76B FoA revenue depends on ad targeting.

7. One Big Beautiful Bill Act CAMT caused a 17pp effective tax rate spike (13% → 30%) — material one-time earnings quality distortion.
[chunk 2/2] KEY FINDINGS from Meta 10-K FY2025 MD&A:

1. HIDDEN LEVERAGE (Severity 4): $103.77B in uncommenced lease obligations sit entirely off-balance-sheet as of Dec 31, 2025. These commence 2026–2030 with terms up to 30 years — a massive shadow liability not yet reflected in the balance sheet lease line.

2. CAPEX ROI GAP (Severity 4): 2026 capex guidance of $115–135B (midpoint ~$125B, ~62% of 2025 revenue) represents ~79% YoY increase from 2025 actual capex of $69.7B. No contracted revenue disclosed to match this spend. Combined with $131.05B in contractual commitments ($30.63B due in 2026 alone), total forward infrastructure obligation is enormous.

3. NON-MARKETABLE EQUITY SCALE (Severity 3): $18.33B deployed into non-marketable equity investments in 2025 alone. Specific investees not named in this section (cross-reference Note 5). Unrealized gains flowing through P&L create earnings volatility.

4. COST OPACITY (Severity 3): Depreciation life extension for servers and network assets effective Jan 1, 2025 artificially suppresses cost of revenue growth rate. Without this change, cost growth and thus operating margin would look materially worse.

5. EXECUTION RISK — Reality Labs (Severity 3): RL lost $19.19B from operations in 2025 (cumulative losses now >$50B+), with non-cancelable purchase commitment losses as an explicit cost driver. RL revenue only $2.21B vs. $19.19B loss.

6. TAX RISK (Severity 3): $15.93B Q3 2025 tax charge including $14.03B DTA valuation allowance driven by OBBBA/CAMT interaction. Effective tax rate jumped from 12% to 30% YoY, materially compressing net income despite record revenue.

7. LONG-TERM DEBT: $59B in senior unsecured notes outstanding (maturing 2027–2064) with $56.74B in future interest obligations — leverage is ramping alongside the capex supercycle.

NOTE: No specific named counterparties for the cloud capacity or lease arrangements were disclosed in this section. Note 5 (Non-Marketable Equity Investments) and Note 7 (Leases) should be extracted separately for full counterparty resolution.

financial_statements_and_notes.notes:
[chunk 1/3] Key extractions from Meta's FY2025 10-K financial statements and notes:

1. VIE / Off-Balance-Sheet: Meta co-developed a data center campus via a "Venture" structured as a VIE. As of 12/31/2025, Meta is NOT the primary beneficiary and does NOT consolidate. This is flagged as a critical audit matter by EY, indicating significant judgment was required. Meta received $2.55B in proceeds from a Venture distribution in 2025, and made $2.43B in payments for held-for-sale assets — suggesting a restructuring or partial exit. The non-consolidated VIE represents hidden leverage.

2. Non-Marketable Equity Investments: Ballooned from $6.07B (2024) to $27.52B (2025), driven by $18.33B in cash purchases in FY2025 alone (vs. $11M in 2024). These are equity-method or measurement-alternative investments in VIEs and private companies, carried off-income-statement. Individual investees are not named in this section (Note 5 referenced but not included in the provided text).

3. CapEx: PP&E purchases of $69.7B in FY2025 (vs. $37.3B in 2024), with $9.33B sitting in accounts payable/accrued liabilities at year-end — a ~87% YoY surge. Large CIP balance not depreciated yet.

4. Depreciation Life Extension (COST_OPACITY): Useful life of servers/network assets extended to 5.5 years in Jan 2025, reducing depreciation expense by $2.92B and boosting net income by $2.59B ($1.00/diluted share). This is a significant non-cash accounting change that inflates reported earnings.

5. Long-Term Debt: Doubled from $28.8B to $58.7B, with $29.9B in new issuances in FY2025.

6. Operating Leases: Total operating lease obligation ~$25.2B ($22.9B non-current + $2.2B current), up from ~$20.2B in 2024.

7. IRS Transfer Pricing: Material uncertain tax position; IRS has applied its position to years beyond those examined.

Note: Note 5 (Non-Marketable Equity Investments) is referenced extensively but the actual investee roster was not included in the provided source text. The $18.33B purchase figure and $27.52B balance are from the cash flow statement and balance sheet respectively.
[chunk 3/3] This section (Notes 12–15, financial statements) contains no off-balance-sheet SPV/VIE disclosures, no named capex commitments to specific counterparties, and no investment footnotes naming private AI lab stakes. Key SIFI-material signals extracted are: (1) Reality Labs cumulative operating loss burn (~$52B over 3 years, $19.2B in 2025) with only $2.2B revenue — severe CAPEX_ROI_GAP; (2) $15.93B one-time CAMT/OBBBA tax charge with $14.03B DTA valuation allowance — COST_OPACITY; (3) IRS asserting $15.89B additional tax for 2017-2019 plus existing $16.45B gross unrecognized tax benefits — material contingent liability with HIDDEN_LEVERAGE characteristics; (4) Long-lived assets surged $60.5B YoY to $196.8B, 88% US-concentrated, corroborating massive capex buildout without matched contracted revenue visibility. No Hyperion SPV or Blue Owl disclosures appear in this specific excerpt — those would appear in earlier notes (Note 7/8 on leases and investments).
